subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance SLO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit@fintechco.com>, Sara Johnson <sara.j@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance SLO recap & next steps

Hi Amit / Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo and the performance SLO discussion so we have alignment on next steps. Please confirm any corrections.

Summary of agreed targets (as discussed):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end inference <= 200 ms for standard chat generation (avg message ~120 tokens).
- Streaming: must support token-by-token streaming for real-time chat UX (low initial-chunk latency).
- Throughput: steady-state ~3k requests/minute; ability to absorb short peaks up to ~5k requests/min.
- Concurrency: support 200–250 concurrent active sessions without degradation.
- Availability & fallbacks: regional failover acceptable; can consider lower-cost model variant for non-critical bursts.

Next actions (Mutual Action Plan):
1) Redwood: share SLO checklist + proposed perf test plan (attached: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx).
2) FintechCo: confirm target traffic profile + provide representative request traces / load CSV (you mentioned infra team will share).
3) Joint: schedule a 90-min perf run (we'll need a sandbox environment or temporary Dedicated pool).
4) Commercial: we'll provide a cost ballpark after initial perf run; will follow with contract draft.

Questions we had for your side:
- Do you have stricter internal p99 latency targets for any sub-paths (e.g., auth, billing lookups) that we should profile separately?
- Preferred window for the perf run next week? We have capacity Wed/Thu mornings (PST).

Attachments: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx, demo recording link (fintechco-demo-recording.mp4) attached for reference.

Cheers,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Priority: p95 latency <= 200 ms is the primary decision criteria; p99 under 400 ms would be nice but is secondary.
- Throughput clarification: the 3k req/min is sustained for core risk-scoring flows; other background workflows are lower priority.
- Concurrency: 250 concurrent sessions is our target for peak trading hours.
- Streaming: required for chat-based customer support; latency to first token should be < 80 ms ideally.

We're pulling together a sample load profile (CSV) and will share via the infra alias by EOD tomorrow. We also want a rough cost estimate scoped to the sustained 3k req/min profile (ballpark $/k tokens + infra).

Decision timeline: our execs want a perf validation and ballpark commercials by 05/21 to decide on pilot.

Attaching a small internal file with recent traffic slices: fintechco-internal-load-profile.csv

Amit Patel

Thanks Amit — great, appreciate the CSV. Quoted for context: 

> We're pulling together a sample load profile (CSV) and will share via the infra alias by EOD tomorrow.

Plan for the perf validation:
- Step 0 (today): ingest your CSV and map to a Redwood load profile.
- Step 1 (Day 1 perf run): synthetic replay of representative traces for 2 hrs to validate p95 / p99 under target concurrency. We'll run both streaming and non-streaming variants.
- Step 2 (Day 2 soak): a 6-hour soak at sustained 3k req/min to validate throughput and memory/KV cache behavior.
- Step 3: regression pass with burst windows up to 5k req/min to ensure graceful fallback.

We can provision a temporary Dedicated pool for the run — Rishi, can you confirm availability for Wed 05/20 (PST morning) and estimate the instance mix you'd use for this profile?

Regarding cost ballpark: we'll prepare an initial estimate post-Day 1 once we see the effective tokens/sec and batching efficiency; I'll flag expected ranges in our follow-up.

Attached: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (checklist + perf test plan). Also linking the demo recording if anyone missed it.

Proposed next meeting: Wed 05/20 @ 9:30am PST — 60–90 min (perf prep + Q&A). Does that work?

Best,
Marissa
